means: a use of a value after it was moved
title: Take the block list out of its box
message: borrow of moved value: `*b`
why: `let v = *b` moved the vector out of the box, so `b` lost R, W and O, and `b.len()` needs R.

fix.why: The vector now lives in `v`, so its length is read from there.

wrong.why: It leaves the box full by copying every block into `v`, only so the length can be read twice.

means: two `&mut` borrows of one place alive at once
title: Append the queue length to the queue
message: cannot borrow `*v` as mutable more than once at a time
why: The reserved `&mut` of `push` allows only reads in the arguments, and `pop` needs W, so it is a second `&mut` of `v`.

fix.why: `pop` finishes in the `if let` head and returns an owned `usize`, so `push` borrows `v` with nothing else alive.

wrong.why: It pops the last id and pushes it onto a copy that is dropped, so the id is lost.

means: a `&mut` borrow while a `&` borrow is alive, or the reverse
title: Append a copy of the queue to itself
message: cannot borrow `*q` as mutable because it is also borrowed as immutable
why: The lazy iterator `ids` still reads `q` and is handed to `extend` on line 3, so `q` lacks W when `extend` needs it.

fix.why: The vector owns its ids, so no borrow of `q` is alive when `extend` needs W.

wrong.why: It extends a copy of the queue and drops it: the real queue never grows.

means: a move out of a value while it is borrowed
title: Peek at a batch head, then hand the batch on
message: cannot move out of `b` because it is borrowed
why: `n` borrows into `b` and is printed on line 4, so `b` has lost O until then (a parameter not declared `mut` never had W), and `push` moves it, which needs O.

fix.why: A `u8` is Copy, so `n` holds a copy and nothing borrows `b` when it moves.

wrong.why: It hands on a copy of every byte in the batch and keeps the original alive only to print one number.

means: an assignment to a place while it is borrowed
title: Peek at the head, then empty the queue
message: cannot assign to `*q` because it is borrowed
why: `head` is a reference into `*q` that line 4 still prints, so `*q` has lost W until then, and assigning a new vector to it needs W.

fix.why: The head is a `u32`, so `head` can hold a copy and no borrow of `*q` is alive at the assignment.

wrong.why: It empties a copy of the queue and drops it, so the real queue keeps every request.

means: a value dropped while something still borrows it
title: Index request ids in a list of views
message: `id` does not live long enough
why: The loop moves each `String` into `id`, which is dropped at the end of its pass, but `ix` keeps a `&str` into it and is read on line 6.

fix.why: Looping over `ids.iter()` lends each id instead of moving it, so the views point into `ids`, which lives until the function returns.

wrong.why: The view is of a copy, and the copy is a temporary dropped at the end of line 4, so `ix` still holds a dangling borrow.

means: a temporary dropped at the end of its statement while still borrowed
title: Trim a label built from an id
message: temporary value dropped while borrowed
why: `to_string()` is a temporary dropped at the end of line 2, but `tag` is a slice into it and is read on later lines.

fix.why: A `&` taken straight in a `let` extends the temporary to the end of the block, so the second `tag` has a `String` to slice.

wrong.why: The trouble is on line 2, where the temporary dies; cloning the slice on line 3 does not keep the `String` alive.

means: a `borrow_mut` on a RefCell that is already borrowed, a panic at run time
title: Bump the queue when a request id is seen
message: RefCell already borrowed
why: In an `if let`, the temporary `Ref` lives until the end of the block, so the cell is still borrowed when `borrow_mut` runs on line 8: the `&mut` rule, checked at run time.

fix.why: The condition of a plain `if` drops its temporary `Ref` before the block runs, so the cell is free again.

wrong.why: Cloning the element changes what the pattern matches on, not when the `Ref` is dropped: it still lives to the end of the block.

means: a returned or stored reference with no lifetime to tie it to
title: Hold a view of the prompt in a lexer
message: missing lifetime specifier
why: A reference stored in a struct must say how long it is valid, and `&str` with no lifetime names nothing the struct could be tied to.

fix.why: The struct declares `'a`, and the field uses it, so every `Lexer` is tied to the text it borrows.

wrong.why: A `'static` field asks for text that lives for the whole program, and `&t` borrows a local `String` that is dropped on return.

means: a closure that may outlive the function while it borrows a local
title: Return the blocks above a minimum size
message: closure may outlive the current function, but it borrows `min`, which is owned by the current function
why: Without `move` the closure borrows the parameter `min`, which is dropped when `above` returns, but the iterator is handed to the caller.

fix.why: `move` copies the `u32` into the closure, so the iterator carries its own `min` out of the function.

wrong.why: The clone is made when the closure runs, and the closure still borrows `min` to reach it: the borrow, and the error, remain.

means: a read of a binding that was never given a value
title: Warm a cache with one id per request
message: used binding `ids` is possibly-uninitialized
why: When `n` is not 0 nothing assigns `ids`, so line 7 moves a binding that holds no value.

fix.why: Each arm now assigns `ids` once, so line 7 always has a vector to return.

wrong.why: It compiles, but the warm cache is empty for every `n`, not `n` ones.

means: a second assignment to a binding not declared `mut`
title: Rotate the active batch for the next one
message: cannot assign to immutable argument `cur`
why: A binding not declared `mut` has no W, and a moved binding does not get one back: `cur = next` is an assignment to it.

fix.text: fn rotate(mut cur: V, next: V) -> V {
fix.why: Declaring the parameter `mut` gives it W, so it can hold a new value after the move.

wrong.text: fn rotate(ref cur: V, next: V) -> V {
wrong.why: `ref` binds a reference to the argument, which is not a `V` any more, and it still gives R only.

means: a use of a value while it is mutably borrowed
title: Bump a depth counter through a reborrow, then read it
message: cannot use `*n` because it was mutably borrowed
why: `m` is still read after `*n`, so `*n` has lent out R and W to the reborrow and reading it lacks R.

fix.why: With `*m` read first, `m` is finished before `*n` is read, so the reborrow is over.

wrong.why: `clone` reads `*n` too, so it needs the same R that `m` has taken, and it copies a `u32` for nothing.

means: a move out of a place behind a reference
title: Take the block list out of its box
message: cannot move out of `*b` which is behind a shared reference
why: Through a `&Box`, `*b` has R but no O, because the caller still owns the box, and `let v = *b` moves the vector out, which needs O.

fix.why: A borrow of the inner vector needs only R, and `len` reads through the reference.

wrong.why: It compiles because it copies every block into a new `Vec`, only to take its length.

means: a move out of an array element by index
title: Add up the lengths of two names in an array
message: cannot move out of type `[String; 2]`, a non-copy array
why: An element of an array has R and W but never O, because rustc cannot track which elements left; `let a = ns[0]` moves the string out.

fix.why: A `&String` needs only R, which every element has.

wrong.why: It copies the first name to read its length.

means: a move out of a field of a type that implements Drop
title: Hand back the address of a closing connection
message: cannot move out of type `Conn`, which implements the `Drop` trait
why: A type with a `Drop` impl must reach `drop` whole, so `c.addr` has R and W but not O; returning the field by value moves it out.

fix.why: It moves the string out and puts an empty one back, so the connection is whole when `drop` runs.

wrong.why: It returns a copy and leaves the original in the connection until `drop` ends it.

means: a returned reference to data the function owns
title: Hand out a view of the first block bytes
message: cannot return value referencing local variable `head`
why: `to_vec` copies the bytes into a `Vec` that `view` owns and drops on return, and the `View` would point into it.

fix.why: The first part of `pool` is a slice of bytes the caller owns, so the `View` can leave the function.

wrong.why: Cloning a slice reference copies the reference, not the bytes, so `head` is the whole pool, not its first four bytes.

means: borrowed data escaping the function
title: Start a worker thread and log its name
message: borrowed data escapes outside of function
why: `move` moves the reference `id` into the thread, but the reference is only valid while the caller's `u32` is, which may end before the thread does.

fix.why: An owned `u32` is copied into the thread, so the thread does not depend on the caller's variable.

wrong.why: It compiles, but callers can now pass only references that live for the whole program, such as a constant, not a counter they own.

means: an assignment through a `&` reference or to a binding not declared `mut`
title: Flush the blocks out of a table
message: cannot assign to `self.epoch`, which is behind a `&` reference
why: Through a `&Table`, `self.epoch` has R but no W, and `+=` writes it.

fix.why: A `&mut self` carries W for every field, so the epoch can change and the blocks can be taken.

wrong.why: The write on line 8 is still behind a `&`, and the copy would leave every block in the table.

means: a `&mut` borrow of a place not declared `mut`
title: Swap the block ids of two tables
message: cannot borrow `b.ids` as mutable, as it is behind a `&` reference
why: Through a `&Table`, `b.ids` has R but no W, and `swap` borrows both places `&mut`.

fix.why: A `&mut Table` carries the W that `swap` needs on both sides.

wrong.why: It reads `b` with R and copies the ids, so `a` gets them but `b` keeps its own and nothing is swapped.

means: a `borrow` on a RefCell that is already mutably borrowed, a panic at run time
title: Record the queue length in the queue
message: RefCell already mutably borrowed
why: The receiver `q.borrow_mut()` runs first and its `RefMut` lives to the end of the statement, so `borrow()` in the argument finds the cell mutably borrowed: R is taken while `&mut` lives.

fix.why: The length was read on line 5 and its `Ref` is gone, so `push` finds the cell free.

wrong.why: It compiles and stops the panic, but it pushes 0 instead of the length that line 5 recorded.
